text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Health officials confiscated 100kg of seal meat at Henties Bay after claims that it had been prepared for human consumption without official permission. Sea Lion Products, which holds the sealing concession at nearby Cape Cross, has denied the accusations saying the meat had been frozen for research.

- The Namibia Agricultural Union (NAU) in its 1997 economic forecast said the projected five percent growth rate for Namibia could only be achieved if there was no drought and if the fishing sector recovered.

- More than 1,400 people have been treated for malaria at the Nankudu hospital in western Kavango since October, including 600 children under the age of five. Malaria cases reported during the first six months of last year increased by 44 percent compared to the same period in 1995.
- Pregnancies among schoolgirls in the Ondangwa east region in northern Namibia reached 1,221 in 1996. Local authorities blamed poverty and a lack of sex education.
